baptism.sub: For the baptism of a child or an adult
baptism.verse: Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
points: New birth
Baptism is not only a name-giving or a family custom. It is a new birth by water and the Spirit: original sin is washed away and the child becomes a child of God.
Into the Church
The baptised person becomes a member of the Body of Christ, the Church. The whole parish receives a new member today.
The white garment and the light

The white garment and the lighted candle are signs of a life to be kept pure and bright. In the Eastern Churches holy Myron (Chrismation) is given together with Baptism, sealing the gift of the Spirit.
Parents and godparents
The promises made today are kept at home: morning and night prayer, the sign of the cross, Sunday {Q}.
homily: Dear parents, godparents and friends, today we bring this child to the font. Jesus said to Nicodemus, “No one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.” What happens here is a birth: the child was born once to you; today the child is born to God.

In Baptism original sin is washed away, and this little one becomes a child of the Father, a brother or sister of Christ, and a temple of the Holy Spirit. The child also becomes a member of the Church. That is why we celebrate it in the church and not only at home: the whole parish receives a new member.

The white garment says: keep this life pure. The burning candle says: keep this light alive. But a candle cannot guard itself. Dear parents and godparents, the promises you make today must be kept in your home: in the first prayers you teach, in the sign of the cross you trace on this forehead, in the Sunday {Q} you never miss.
Let us thank God for this child, and let us all renew our own Baptism today. Each of us was once carried to the font like this. May we live as children of God. Amen.
baptism.prayer: Heavenly Father, you have given this child a new birth by water and the Spirit. Keep the white garment unstained and the light of faith burning, and bless the parents and godparents who will lead this child to you. Amen.

communion.sub: For the day children receive the Body and Blood of the Lord for the first time
communion.verse: I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
points: Not a sign only
What the children receive today looks like bread, but it is truly the Body and Blood of Jesus, given for them.
The manna and the true bread
God fed Israel in the desert with manna; Jesus gives himself as the bread that gives eternal life.
A first, not a last
The danger is that First Communion becomes the last. Ask parents to bring the children every Sunday.
Prepared hearts
Confession, the fast before Communion, reverence and thanksgiving afterwards.
homily: Dear children, today is one of the most beautiful days of your life. For many weeks you have prepared, learnt your prayers and made your first Confession. Today Jesus himself comes to live in your heart.

When the priest gives you the Holy Communion, it will look like bread. But Jesus said, “I am the bread of life.” It is really Jesus: his Body and Blood, his whole self, with all his love. In the desert God gave the people manna; today he gives you his own Son.

When you receive Jesus, close your eyes and speak to him. Thank him. Tell him about your family, your friends, your fears. He is listening. And remember: this is your first Holy Communion, not your last! Jesus wants to meet you every Sunday.
Dear parents, the beautiful clothes and photographs will soon be put away. Please do not put away the {Q}. Bring your children every Sunday, and receive with them. Amen.
communion.prayer: Lord Jesus, bread of life, today these children receive you for the first time. Stay in their hearts, make them hungry for you every Sunday, and keep them always close to you. Amen.

confirmation.sub: For the celebration of the sacrament of Confirmation
confirmation.verse: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
points: The seal of the Spirit
Confirmation completes the grace of Baptism. The bishop anoints with chrism: “Be sealed with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.”
The seven gifts
Wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety and fear of the Lord (Isaiah 11:2).
Witnesses
Not a graduation from the Church, but a sending into the world as witnesses.
A practical gift
Name one place where each young person will need courage this year: school, friends, social media.
homily: Dear young people, today the Holy Spirit comes upon you in a new way. You were baptised as infants; others spoke for you. Today you say your own “yes”, and the Church seals you with the Gift of the Holy Spirit.

At Pentecost the frightened apostles became bold witnesses. The same Spirit gives you his seven gifts: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety and fear of the Lord. These are not ornaments; they are tools for life.

Confirmation is sometimes treated as the end of catechism, the day after which we need not come to church. It is exactly the opposite. Jesus says, “You will be my witnesses.” You are being sent: to your school, your friends, your phone, your future work.
Ask the Holy Spirit today for one gift you need most. And come back next Sunday to the {Q}, where the Spirit keeps strengthening you. Amen.
confirmation.prayer: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of these young people. Seal them with your gifts, make them brave witnesses of Christ, and keep them faithful all their lives. Amen.

betrothal.sub: For the betrothal or engagement in church before marriage
betrothal.verse: It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper as his partner.
points: A free consent
The heart of the betrothal is a free promise. No one may be forced; the Church asks, and each answers freely.
God's plan from the beginning
“It is not good that the man should be alone.” Marriage is God's idea before it is ours.
Love that is patient
1 Corinthians 13 describes love as a decision, not only a feeling.
The time of preparation
Prayer together, the marriage preparation course, a good Confession, honesty about finances and families, and chastity.
homily: Dear brother and sister, today you stand before God and his Church and declare your intention to marry. This is not yet the wedding, but it is a holy beginning. The Church asks you whether you come freely, and you answer for yourselves.

In the very first pages of the Bible God says: “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper as his partner.” Your love is not an accident. It belongs to God's plan from the beginning.

The weeks before a wedding are often filled with halls, dresses, food and invitations. Do not let them steal the real preparation. Pray together. Take the marriage preparation course seriously. Speak honestly about your families, your money and your hopes. Make a good Confession before the wedding.
St Paul tells us that love is patient and kind, that it bears all things and hopes all things. Ask God for that love now, and you will carry it into your marriage. Amen.
betrothal.prayer: Lord God, you created man and woman for each other. Bless these two who have promised to marry; prepare their hearts by your grace, and lead them in purity and joy to the day of their wedding. Amen.

marriage.verse: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
points: A covenant, not a contract
Marriage is a covenant of the whole life, sealed before God; for the baptised it is a sacrament.
Christ and the Church
St Paul compares the love of husband and wife to the love of Christ for his Church: faithful, self-giving, to the cross.
One, faithful, for ever
“What God has joined together, let no one separate.” Unity, fidelity, openness to life.
Invite Jesus
At Cana the wine ran out. In every marriage it sometimes does. Keep Jesus and Mary at the table.
homily: Dear bride and bridegroom, dear families, today two lives become one. Jesus said: “They are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.” What happens at this altar is not only a promise between you; it is God himself joining you.

Marriage is a covenant, not a contract. A contract says, “I will give as long as you give.” A covenant says, “I give myself, whatever comes.” St Paul tells husbands and wives to love as Christ loved the Church. And how did Christ love? To the cross.

At Cana the wine ran out in the middle of the wedding. In every marriage, at some time, the wine runs out: patience, money, health, feelings. Do what Mary said: “Do whatever he tells you.” Keep Jesus in your home. Pray together every day. Forgive before you sleep. Come together to the {Q}.
Dear families, support this new home with your prayers and your respect, not with interference. And may God, who began this good work in you today, bring it to completion. Amen.
marriage.prayer: Lord God, you have joined these two in holy marriage. Make their love faithful and fruitful, keep Jesus and Mary in their home, and when the wine runs short, fill their jars again. Amen.

ordination.sub: For an ordination or a new priest's first celebration
ordination.verse: You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last.
points: Chosen, not self-made
A priest does not choose himself; Christ chooses and the Church calls through the bishop.
Taken from among the people
“Every high priest chosen from among mortals is put in charge of things pertaining to God on their behalf” (Hebrews 5:1). He remains one of us and is given for us.
In the person of Christ
At the altar and in the confessional, the priest acts in the person of Christ the Head. The gift is greater than the man.
The family and the parish
Thank the parents who gave a son; pray for vocations from this parish.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is a day of great joy for this parish and this family. One of our own stands at the altar as a priest of Jesus Christ. Jesus says to him: “You did not choose me but I chose you.”

A priest is taken from among the people and given back to the people. He is not an angel; he is a son of this soil, with his own weaknesses. That is exactly why God's choice is so moving. Through his hands bread and wine will become the Body and Blood of Christ; through his words sins will be forgiven. The gift is far greater than the man.

Dear new priest, Jesus appointed you “to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last.” The fruit that lasts is not buildings or popularity; it is souls brought to God. Stay close to the Lord in prayer, love the poor, and never be ashamed to ask for forgiveness.
Dear parents, thank you for giving your son to God. Dear parish, pray for him every day, and pray that more of your sons and daughters will hear the call. Amen.
ordination.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal High Priest, you have chosen this servant for your altar. Keep him holy, humble and joyful; make his priesthood bear fruit that will last, and raise up many more labourers for your harvest. Amen.

profession.sub: For first or final vows of a religious brother or sister
profession.verse: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot.
points: Everything for Christ
“Whatever gains I had, these I have come to regard as loss because of Christ” (Philippians 3:7).
Three vows
Poverty, chastity and obedience: not a loss of life, but a life given wholly to God.
A sign for all
Religious life reminds every Christian that God alone is enough and that heaven is our home.
Gratitude
Thank the family and the community; pray for perseverance.
homily: Dear sister (brother), today you give your whole life to God by the vows of poverty, chastity and obedience. With the psalmist you say: “The Lord is my chosen portion and my cup.”

In the Gospel a rich young man came to Jesus and went away sad, because he could not let go. Today we see the opposite: someone who has heard “Come, follow me” and says yes. St Paul says, “I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.”

The vows are not chains. Poverty sets you free from possessions; chastity sets your heart free to love everyone; obedience sets you free from yourself. And your life becomes a sign for all of us that God alone is enough.
Dear family, you are not losing a daughter (son); you are giving her (him) to God, and God is never outdone in generosity. Let us pray that she (he) may be faithful to the end. Amen.
profession.prayer: Lord, you are the portion and the cup of your servant. Accept the offering of this life, keep her (him) faithful to the vows professed today, and make her (his) joy a witness to your love. Amen.

sick.t: Anointing and Prayer for the Sick
sick.sub: For the anointing of the sick, or a Mass or prayer service for the sick
sick.verse: Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points: Not only for the dying
The anointing of the sick is for anyone seriously ill, before surgery, or weakened by old age (CCC 1514).
The Lord's own sacrament
“Are any among you sick? They should call for the elders of the church and have them pray over them, anointing them with oil in the name of the Lord” (James 5:14).
Grace in suffering
Strength, peace and courage; forgiveness of sins; union with the Passion of Christ; healing of body if it is God's will.
The community cares
Visiting, bringing Communion, helping the family.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, especially you who are sick, Jesus says to you today: “Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.” You are not forgotten. You are at the centre of the Church's prayer.

Many people think the anointing of the sick is only for the dying, and so they call the priest too late. It is not so. St James says: “Are any among you sick? They should call for the elders of the church.” This sacrament is for anyone seriously ill, before an operation, or weakened by age.

What does the sacrament give? Peace and courage; the forgiveness of sins; the grace to unite your suffering with the suffering of Christ; and, if it is God's will, healing of the body. Isaiah says of Jesus: “By his bruises we are healed.” Your pain, joined to his, is never wasted.
And to the families and the parish: the sick need our presence. Visit them, sit with them, bring them Holy Communion, help those who care for them. That too is the Church at prayer. Amen.
sick.prayer: Lord Jesus, you took our infirmities and bore our diseases. Look on your servants who are sick: give them strength and peace, forgive their sins, unite their suffering with your Passion, and, if it is your will, restore them to health. Amen.

funeral.sub: For the funeral of a Christian
funeral.verse: I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live.
points: Grief is not faithless
Jesus wept at the tomb of Lazarus. Tears are allowed; despair is not.
Christ has conquered death
“I am the resurrection and the life.” Death is not the end but a passage.
We pray for the dead
The Church has always prayed and offered the Eucharist for the departed, that they may be purified and enter the joy of God (CCC 1032; 2 Maccabees 12:46).
Speak of the person truthfully
Remember the life with gratitude, without exaggeration; the focus is Christ's mercy.
homily: Dear family and friends, we have come together with heavy hearts to say farewell to our brother (sister) N. At the tomb of his friend Lazarus, Jesus wept. So we too may weep today. Christian faith does not forbid tears; it gives them hope.

To Martha, standing in her grief, Jesus said: “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live.” These are the words we hold on to today. For the believer, death is not a wall but a door. Christ has passed through it before us and has broken its power.

We remember N. with gratitude: for his (her) love, his (her) work, his (her) faith. But we do not canonise anyone at a funeral. We entrust him (her) to the mercy of God. From the earliest times the Church has prayed and offered the Eucharist for the dead, so that they may be purified and enter fully into God's joy. That is the greatest gift we can still give: our prayer.
Dear family, you are not alone. The parish stands with you. And one day, by God's mercy, we hope to meet again where every tear will be wiped away. Eternal rest grant unto him (her), O Lord. Amen.
funeral.prayer: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, receive our brother (sister) N. into your mercy. Forgive his (her) sins, bring him (her) into the light of your face, and console all who mourn with the hope of the resurrection. Amen.

memorial.t: Commemoration of the Departed (41st day, anniversary)
memorial.sub: For the 41st-day remembrance, a death anniversary or a memorial Mass
memorial.verse: In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. If it were not so, would I have told you that I go to prepare a place for you?
points: Love does not end
Death separates us for a time; it does not break the communion of saints.
Why we offer the Eucharist
The {Q} offered for the departed is the greatest help we can give them (CCC 1032, 1371).
Remember to imitate
Recall one virtue of the departed and ask the family to carry it on.
Our own preparation
Every remembrance is also a reminder: live today ready to meet the Lord.
homily: Dear family and friends, we have gathered again to remember N. The days have passed, the first tears have perhaps become quieter, but the love remains. And love, in Christ, does not end.

Jesus says: “In my Father's house there are many dwelling places.” Our dear ones have not disappeared; they have gone ahead. We believe in the communion of saints: those on earth, those being purified, and those in heaven form one family in Christ.

That is why we offer this {Q} for N. The Church teaches that the Eucharistic sacrifice is offered also for the faithful departed, that they may enter the light and peace of Christ. Our prayer is the most precious gift we can still give.

Let us also remember to imitate. Think of one good thing N. did, and continue it in your own life. And let each of us live today in such a way that we are ready to meet the Lord. Eternal rest grant unto him (her), O Lord. Amen.
memorial.prayer: Lord, in your Father's house there are many dwelling places. Grant N. a place of light and peace, and keep us faithful, so that one day we may all be gathered together in your kingdom. Amen.

weddingjubilee.sub: For the silver, golden or any anniversary of marriage
weddingjubilee.verse: But you have kept the good wine until now.
points: The good wine kept until now
At Cana the best wine came last. Years of faithful love can become better, not weaker.
Grace, not only effort
A long marriage is a work of God's grace as much as of human effort.
Forgiveness as daily bread
“Bear with one another and… forgive each other” (Colossians 3:13).
A witness to the young
In a time of broken families, faithful couples preach without words.
homily: Dear N. and N., today we thank God with you for these years of married life. At Cana the steward said: “Everyone serves the good wine first… But you have kept the good wine until now.” Your jubilee is that good wine.

When you stood at the altar years ago, you could not know everything that was coming: children, joys, illnesses, debts, misunderstandings, reconciliations. But you kept your promise. That is not only your achievement; it is God's grace working in two ordinary hearts.

St Paul describes the secret: “Bear with one another and, if anyone has a complaint against another, forgive each other; just as the Lord has forgiven you.” Forgiveness was your daily bread. Teach that to your children and grandchildren.
In a time when many marriages break, your faithfulness is a sermon without words. May the Lord who kept the best wine until now give you many more years together. Amen.
weddingjubilee.prayer: Lord Jesus, guest at Cana, we thank you for the years of love you have given N. and N. Renew their love, bless their children and grandchildren, and keep the best wine for the years still to come. Amen.

priestjubilee.sub: For the jubilee of a priest or a religious
priestjubilee.verse: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me?
points: Gratitude first
The psalmist answers his own question: “I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD” (Psalm 116:13).
Treasure in clay jars
“We have this treasure in clay jars, so that it may be made clear that this extraordinary power belongs to God” (2 Corinthians 4:7).
“Do you love me?”
Peter's threefold question is the question of every jubilee: love renewed after years of service and failure.
Thank the people
A priest's or religious's life is woven with the people they served.
homily: Dear Father (Sister) N., dear friends, today we join the psalmist in asking: “What shall I return to the Lord for all his bounty to me?” And the psalm answers: “I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.” For a priest that is exactly what happens every day at the altar.

St Paul says: “We have this treasure in clay jars.” After many years of service, a jubilarian knows better than anyone how fragile the jar is, and how great the treasure. The fruit of these years belongs to God.

By the lake, the risen Jesus asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” Peter had failed him, and yet Jesus entrusted his sheep to him again. Every jubilee is that question renewed: after all these years, do you love me? And the answer is: “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.”
Let us thank God for this life given, and let us pray that our families may give more sons and daughters to the service of the Lord. Amen.
priestjubilee.prayer: Lord, we thank you for the years of service of your servant N. Renew the grace of the first day, forgive what was lacking, and keep him (her) faithful in love until the end. Amen.

parishfeast.sub: For the patronal feast (perunnal), the dedication anniversary or the jubilee of a parish or institution
read: Matthew 5:1–12 or the Gospel of the patron saint
parishfeast.verse: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the LORD!”
points: Why we celebrate a saint
The patron is a friend and intercessor who points to Christ, not a substitute for him.
A family of faith
The parish is the family of families: “citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God” (Ephesians 2:19).
The real decoration
Lights, processions and fireworks pass; confession, charity and reconciliation remain. Keep a share of the feast for the poor.
Looking forward
A jubilee looks back with thanks and forward with mission: who is missing from our parish today?
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the psalmist says: “I was glad when they said to me, Let us go to the house of the Lord!” Today our parish is glad. We celebrate our patron (our jubilee), and the whole family of the parish has come home.

Why do we honour a saint? Not because the saint replaces Christ, but because the saint shows us Christ. Our patron walked the road we walk and reached the goal. He (she) is our friend in heaven, praying for this parish.

Our feast has lights, processions, music and food, and that is good. But the real decoration of a feast is a cleansed heart: a good Confession, a family reconciled, a poor neighbour remembered. Let a share of this feast reach those who cannot celebrate.

And let us look forward. Who is missing from our parish today? Whom can we invite back? May our patron intercede for us, so that this parish may be a living house of God for the generations to come. Amen.
parishfeast.prayer: Lord God, we thank you for our parish and for the faith handed down to us. Through the intercession of our patron, make us one family in Christ, generous to the poor and faithful to the end. Amen.

house.sub: For the blessing of a new house (house warming)
house.verse: …but as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD.
points: Unless the Lord builds the house
“Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain” (Psalm 127:1).
Salvation came to Zacchaeus' house
“Today salvation has come to this house” (Luke 19:9): Jesus enters, and the household changes.
A domestic church
The home is where faith is first learnt: the prayer corner, the family rosary or evening prayer, the Bible on the table.
An open door
Hospitality to the poor and to guests is a blessing on the house.
homily: Dear family, today we bless this new home. Many years of work and saving are in these walls. But the psalm reminds us: “Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.” Today you invite the Lord to be the true builder.

When Jesus entered the house of Zacchaeus, he said: “Today salvation has come to this house.” A house is blessed not only by holy water but by the presence of Christ. Let him enter every room: the kitchen, the bedroom, the study, and especially the place of family prayer.

Joshua stood before the people and said: “As for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.” Make that your family motto. Keep a prayer corner, pray together every evening, keep the Bible open, and let the children see their parents kneel.
And keep your door open to guests and to the poor. A house that welcomes is a house that God fills with blessing. Peace be to this house and to all who live in it. Amen.
house.prayer: Lord Jesus, as you entered the house of Zacchaeus, enter this home. Bless all who live here and all who visit, keep sickness, quarrels and every evil far from it, and make it a home of prayer, peace and welcome. Amen.

school.t: Beginning of the School or Academic Year
school.sub: For a school Mass, the start of the academic year, or before examinations
school.verse: And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points: Ask for wisdom, like Solomon
Solomon asked not for riches but for “an understanding mind” (1 Kings 3:9).
Jesus grew
“Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor” (Luke 2:52): grow in all three.
Think about what is good
“Whatever is true, whatever is honorable… think about these things” (Philippians 4:8).
Teachers and parents
Thank teachers; parents are the first teachers.
homily: Dear children, dear teachers, a new year of learning begins. When God asked young King Solomon what he wanted, Solomon did not ask for riches or for victory over his enemies. He asked for wisdom, “an understanding mind”. God was so pleased that he gave him that and much more.

St Luke tells us that the boy Jesus “increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.” Notice the three things: wisdom, which is learning; years, which is growing up; and favour with God and people, which is goodness. A good student grows in all three.

St Paul gives a simple rule for the mind: “Whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure… think about these things.” What you watch and read and think shapes who you become.
Let us thank God for our teachers and our parents, and let us begin this year asking, like Solomon, for wisdom. Amen.
school.prayer: Lord Jesus, you grew in wisdom and in favour with God and people. Bless our students, teachers and parents this year; give us understanding minds, honest work and kind hearts. Amen.
